title: Every Time I Lie, My Dad's Nose Grows 🤥
lines: My dad was reading the weather on live TV when his nose shot through the screen and knocked over a camera.
That was my fault. I had just told my mom I cleaned my room.
You see, two weeks earlier, I found out about the rule. Every time I lie, my dad's nose grows.
I told my teacher my dog ate my homework. Across town, Dad's nose popped a balloon at a kid's birthday party.
I told Grandma her fruitcake was delicious. Dad's nose rang a church bell.
So I made a plan. I would stop lying. Completely.
Attempt one. I stopped talking. Mom asked if I was okay. I nodded. Dad's nose grew anyway.
Attempt two. I taped my mouth shut. A kid asked if I liked his drawing. I gave him a thumbs up.
Dad's nose knocked a helicopter out of the sky. A toy helicopter. Still.
Attempt three. Only the truth. All the time.
Do you like my new haircut?
I said it looked like a mop. I told the principal he smells like soup.
I got detention. The principal started wearing cologne. It smells like soup.
But Dad's nose kept growing. Even when I didn't say anything.
It grew every night at seven. Exactly when Dad called to say goodnight from the TV station.
Sorry, buddy. Busy night. I'll make it up to you.
I said, "It's fine. I don't care."
That's when I figured it out. "I don't care" was the biggest lie I ever told.
Dad had missed my last six games, my birthday, and the science fair. Every time, I said it was fine.
So the next morning, I went to the TV station. Dad was about to go live. His nose was already three feet long.
Ten seconds! Somebody shorten his nose!
I walked right onto the set.
Dad, I do care. I miss you. I want you at my game.
His nose went pop and shrank back to normal. On live TV. In front of two million people.
Dad looked at the camera. Then at me. Then he took off his microphone.
Today's forecast: a hundred percent chance I'm going to my son's game.
He walked off the set. The producer fainted.
He made it to the game. He cheered so loud the referee gave him a yellow card.
We lost by twenty points. Best game of my life.
Now I don't lie anymore. Not even small ones.
Which brings us back to the weather.
Last night, Dad said tomorrow would be sunny. It snowed two feet.
His nose didn't grow. He's just bad at weather.
